newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 16.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 16. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Some 11,000 of Indonesia's 17,508 islands have not been named. Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago.
Indonesian police have arrested a South African national for allegedly trying to smuggle 333 grammes of morphine, which was found in his stomach.

Director-General for Social and Political Affairs Sutoyo N.K. critised the central Java administration's controversial policy to paint public facilities in yellow, the official colour of the ruling Golkar party. General elections are scheduled in May.
Members of the House of Representatives have urged Indonesian businessmen to help close the wealth gap - an issue which has sparked a number of riots in the multi-ethnic country.

The government will renovate the headquarters of the divided Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) which was badly damaged after being stormed by supporters of the party's government-backed leader Surjadi on July 27. The headquarters until then was occupied by backers of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
